evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into logistics probing without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer that required follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep says: 'I'm getting this moved including the drive probably between three to four hours... We would be looking at cost wise between $805 and probably about $1,035.' Anchored to typical range for this move size and personalized to the drive time and straightforward nature.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee disclosed: '$115 trip fee since we're moving from Austin to Leander.' Two-and-a-half-hour minimum mentioned: 'we do have a two and a half hour minimum and you do only pay for the time that you use.' However, '15-minute increments' framing and 'not a guess' commitment framing are absent.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' or similar validation question.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. Instead, rep says: 'Completely up to you if you want to go ahead and reserve that free truck you can.' This is a soft, optional framing with an easy out, but the underlying ask is also never explicitly stated.

top_strength: Chauntelle gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, floor level, proximity to door, detailed inventory, destination address, delivery location details) and provided a personalized, anchored estimate ($805–$1,035 for 3–4 hours including drive and trip fee) that felt accurate and grounded in the customer's actual move profile.
coaching_note: Section 2's 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' must be asked before any logistics probing starts; Section 5's Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) were entirely skipped; and Section 7's explicit ask for the business ('Would you like our help?') was never plainly stated—these three structural gaps are the primary gaps holding this call back from passing.
